userStories.title: Add flake probe module and flakeDetection config
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build the isolation re-run mechanic and its config surface for flaky-test detection.

**Motivation** — A flaky pre-existing test in the target repo currently burns real money and time: nax attributes the intermittent failure to the agent's change, dispatches rectification fix cycles, escalates model tiers, and can fail the regression gate — all for a failure the story did not cause.

**Approach** — **`src/verification/flake-probe.ts`** — the re-run mechanic. Input: a `TestFailure`, the detected `Framework`, the package's base test command (from `config.quality.commands.test`, per-package resolved — never hardcoded), a working directory, and probe config. Builds an isolation command by combining the base command with a framework-specific filter:

| Framework | Filter shape (appended to / derived from base command) |
|---|---|
| bun | `<base> <file> -t <escaped name>` |
| jest / vitest | `<base> <file> -t <escaped name>` |
| pytest | `<base> <file>::<name>` |
| go | `<base> -run '^<escaped name>$'` scoped to the failing package |

Test names are escaped for `-t`/`-run` regex metacharacters. Executes via `executeWithTimeout` with `probeTimeoutSeconds` and the package `cwd`. Returns a discriminated verdict:

- `{ verdict: "flaky", probeRuns, probePasses }` — passed at least once
- `{ verdict: "consistent-failure", probeRuns }` — failed every probe
- `{ verdict: "unprobeable", reason }` — `file === "unknown"`, `framework === "unknown"`, or no filter command can be constructed

A probe run counts as a pass only on a clean pass; crash, environmental-failure classification, or timeout counts as a failed probe.

**Scope** — In: `src/verification/flake-probe.ts`, `src/verification/index.ts`, `src/config/schemas-execution.ts`, and the execution config merge path needed to make `flakeDetection` package-overridable. Out: baseline classification, run-scoped quarantine memoization, story-orchestrator wiring, and regression attribution changes.

**Interface**
```typescript
{ verdict: "flaky", probeRuns, probePasses }
{ verdict: "consistent-failure", probeRuns }
{ verdict: "unprobeable", reason }
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given nax config with `execution.flakeDetection` unset, when the config is constructed, then resolved `execution.flakeDetection.enabled` is `true`, `probeRuns` is `2`, `maxProbesPerGate` is `5`, and `probeTimeoutSeconds` is `60`.
When `runFlakeProbe` is imported from `src/verification`, then it is available as a callable function.

Given framework `bun`, `jest`, or `vitest`, when `runFlakeProbe` receives a base test command and a failing test `{ file, testName }`, then the isolation command starts from the provided base command and includes both the test file path and a name filter for the test.
Given framework `pytest`, when `runFlakeProbe` builds an isolation command for a failing test, then the command addresses the single test as `<file>::<testName>`.
Given framework `go`, when `runFlakeProbe` builds an isolation command for a failing test, then the command uses an anchored run filter `^…$` for the test name.

Given a test name containing regex metacharacters such as `handles (edge) case?`, when `runFlakeProbe` builds a name filter, then the metacharacters are escaped so the filter selects the test name literally.

Given the executor dependency is stubbed so the first probe run fails and the second passes, when `runFlakeProbe` runs with `probeRuns = 2`, then it returns `{ verdict: "flaky" }` with `probeRuns == 2` and `probePasses == 1`.
Given the executor dependency is stubbed so every probe run fails, when `runFlakeProbe` completes, then it returns verdict `consistent-failure`.

Given a failing test whose `file` is `"unknown"`, or a detected framework of `"unknown"`, when `runFlakeProbe` is called, then it returns verdict `unprobeable` and never invokes the executor dependency.
Given one probe run returns a timeout or environmental failure and one probe run returns a clean pass, when `runFlakeProbe` runs two probes, then it returns verdict `flaky` with `probePasses == 1`.
Given all probe runs return only timeouts or environmental failures, when `runFlakeProbe` completes, then it returns verdict `consistent-failure`.

routing.reasoning: The story adds one new verification helper and additive execution config on top of existing executor and detector seams, so standard multi-file TDD is sufficient.

suggestedCriteria: Given a root config with `execution.flakeDetection` values and a package override that changes only `probeRuns`, when `mergePackageConfig()` merges them, then the merged config keeps the root `enabled`, `maxProbesPerGate`, and `probeTimeoutSeconds` values while using the package override for `probeRuns`.

userStories.title: Add flaky finding triage and run-scoped memoization
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build the classifier that decides when `failed-test` findings become run-scoped `flaky-test` quarantines.

**Motivation** — No re-run-the-failing-test logic exists anywhere in the codebase today; every existing re-run (rectification loop, regression gate, acceptance loop) re-runs a whole scope after an attempted edit, never "run this same failing test again unchanged to see if it flips."

**Approach** — **`src/verification/flake-triage.ts`** — the classifier and sole decision-maker. Input: `failed-test` findings + story context (diff, config, workdir/packageDir, run-scoped quarantine memo). Per finding: baseline check → probe → relabel. Output: the same findings array with confirmed flakes relabeled to `category: "flaky-test"` and `meta: { probeRuns, probePasses }`, plus a quarantine report (keys, reasons) for logging/events. Per `src/findings/types.ts`, `meta` is forensic-only — all downstream branching (fix-strategy `appliesTo`, `gateFailureKeys` exclusion, attribution) discriminates on `category`, never on `meta` fields. Maintains a run-scoped in-memory memo keyed `${file}::${testName}` so the regression gate does not re-probe tests already judged flaky earlier in the run. Skips probing entirely (all findings stay blocking, reason logged) when distinct failed pre-existing tests at one gate exceed `maxProbesPerGate`.

Detection = two signals that must both agree:

1. **Baseline check (cheap, first):** the failing test is pre-existing and untouched — its test file is not in the story's diff and is not mapped from changed sources.
2. **Isolation probe (expensive, second):** the test passes at least once when re-run alone `probeRuns` times.

Fail closed everywhere: unprobeable or ambiguous outcomes keep the finding blocking.

**Scope** — In: `src/verification/flake-triage.ts`, barrel export wiring, baseline checks against diff and source→test mapping, quarantine memo behavior, and triage error handling. Out: story-orchestrator integration, regression-gate attribution changes, and probe command construction itself.

**Interface**
```typescript
Input: failed-test findings + story context (diff, config, workdir/packageDir, run-scoped quarantine memo)
Output: findings array with confirmed flakes relabeled to category: "flaky-test" and meta: { probeRuns, probePasses }, plus a quarantine report
Key: `${file}::${testName}`
```
acceptanceCriteria: When `triageFlakyFindings` is imported from `src/verification` and called with an empty findings array, then it returns an empty findings array and an empty quarantine report.

Given `runFlakeProbe` is stubbed, when `triageFlakyFindings` receives a `failed-test` finding for a pre-existing test that is absent from the story diff and unmapped from changed sources, then it invokes the stub exactly once with that test's file, test name, and resolved `flakeDetection` config.

Given a `failed-test` finding whose test file appears in the story's changed files, when `triageFlakyFindings` runs, then it does not invoke the probe dependency and the finding keeps `category: "failed-test"`.

Given a `failed-test` finding whose test file is mapped from a changed source file, when `triageFlakyFindings` runs, then it does not invoke the probe dependency and the finding keeps `category: "failed-test"`.
Given a probed finding with verdict `flaky`, when `triageFlakyFindings` returns it, then the finding has `category: "flaky-test"` and populated `meta.probeRuns` and `meta.probePasses`.
Given a probed finding with verdict `consistent-failure`, when `triageFlakyFindings` returns it, then the finding keeps `category: "failed-test"`.

Given a finding whose key `${file}::${testName}` is already present in the run-scoped quarantine memo, when `triageFlakyFindings` runs, then it relabels the finding to `flaky-test` without invoking the probe dependency again.

Given the number of distinct probe candidates at one gate exceeds `maxProbesPerGate`, when `triageFlakyFindings` runs, then it never invokes the probe dependency, every finding keeps `category: "failed-test"`, and the quarantine report records the skip reason.
Given `execution.flakeDetection.enabled == false`, when `triageFlakyFindings` runs, then it returns findings unchanged and never invokes the probe dependency.
Given the probe dependency throws, when `triageFlakyFindings` runs, then it does not propagate the exception and the affected finding keeps `category: "failed-test"`.

routing.reasoning: The story adds one new classifier module that composes existing diff, resolver, and smart-runner helpers with fail-closed branching, which fits normal multi-file TDD.

suggestedCriteria: Given `triageFlakyFindings` receives findings whose `source` or `category` are not eligible for flaky classification, when it returns, then those findings are passed through unchanged.

userStories.title: Integrate flaky triage into the full-suite gate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply flaky-test triage to per-story full-suite gate failures before rectification and phase-regression comparisons.

**Motivation** — A flaky pre-existing test in the target repo currently burns real money and time: nax attributes the intermittent failure to the agent's change, dispatches rectification fix cycles, escalates model tiers, and can fail the regression gate — all for a failure the story did not cause.

**Approach** — Wire triage into per-story rectification; gate pass-with-warnings; phase-eval exclusions.

`gatherRectificationFindings(...)` / `runRectification(...)` — `src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts`. Triage runs on gate findings before they reach the fix cycle.

`gateFailureKeys(gateOutput)` and `gateRegressedAfterRectification(...)` — `src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts`. Key shape `${file}::${rule}` where `rule` is the testName; both must skip `flaky-test` findings.

Existing precedent for the philosophy: `shouldSkipPhaseForRectification()` (same file as `gatherRectificationFindings`) already treats a failing gate with a passing verifier as an unrelated pre-existing regression.

**Scope** — In: story-orchestrator rectification wiring, fix-cycle input filtering, gate warning behavior, and `phase-eval` exclusion logic for `flaky-test`. Out: probe implementation, baseline detection internals, and deferred regression attribution.

**Interface**
```typescript
Seam: the triage entry point (new export) is called from story-orchestrator rectification.
Input: the gate's failed-test findings before the fix cycle sees them.
Key shape: `${file}::${rule}` where `rule` is the testName.
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given the triage dependency is stubbed, when a full-suite-gate failure is processed, then exactly one triage invocation occurs with the gate's `failed-test` findings before rectification findings are gathered.

Given triage relabels every gate failure to `flaky-test` and there are no other blocking findings, when the full-suite gate result is handled, then no fix cycle is dispatched for that gate, one warning is recorded per quarantined test, and the story remains passing.
Given triage returns a mix of `flaky-test` and `failed-test` findings, when rectification is dispatched, then the fix cycle receives only the `failed-test` findings.
When `gateFailureKeys` is called with gate output containing `flaky-test` findings, then the returned key set excludes those `flaky-test` findings.
Given baseline and final gate findings differ only by `flaky-test` findings, when `gateRegressedAfterRectification` is evaluated, then it reports no regression.
Given a quarantine decision at the full-suite gate, when it is logged, then the structured log entry includes the story id and the quarantined test key `${file}::${testName}`.

routing.reasoning: This work is limited to wiring one new triage step into existing rectification and phase-eval paths that already have focused unit-test seams.

userStories.title: Integrate flaky triage into deferred regression
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply run-scoped flaky-test quarantine to deferred regression before story attribution and regression rectification.

**Motivation** — A flaky pre-existing test in the target repo currently burns real money and time: nax attributes the intermittent failure to the agent's change, dispatches rectification fix cycles, escalates model tiers, and can fail the regression gate — all for a failure the story did not cause.

**Approach** — Wire triage into the deferred regression gate; exclude flakes from story attribution; success-with-warnings; shared memo.

`runDeferredRegression(options: DeferredRegressionOptions)` + internal `buildRegressionFindings(...)`, `findResponsibleStoryByTransition(...)`, `_regressionDeps` DI object — `src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts`.

The triage entry point is called from `runDeferredRegression` on regression failures with the shared run-scoped memo.

A test quarantined earlier in the same run is relabeled at the regression gate without a new probe invocation.

**Scope** — In: deferred regression triage invocation, DI seam updates, affected-story filtering, warning/success result shaping, and shared memo threading from earlier gate quarantines. Out: probe command mechanics and per-story full-suite gate integration.

**Interface**
```typescript
runDeferredRegression(options: DeferredRegressionOptions): Promise<DeferredRegressionResult>
buildRegressionFindings(summary: TestSummary, rawOutput: string): Finding[]
Seam: triage is stubbed into the regression module's DI seam and invoked on regression failed-test findings with the shared run-scoped memo.
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given the triage dependency is stubbed into the regression module DI seam, when a deferred regression suite fails, then `runDeferredRegression` invokes triage with the regression run's `failed-test` findings.

Given every regression failure is relabeled to `flaky-test`, when `runDeferredRegression` completes, then it returns `success: true` and the returned quarantine report lists each quarantined test key as a warning.
Given a test is relabeled `flaky-test`, when regression attribution runs, then no story is attributed and no fix cycle is dispatched on the basis of that quarantined test alone.
Given one genuine regression failure and one quarantined flake, when deferred regression runs, then exactly one per-story fix cycle is dispatched for the story attributed to the genuine failure.
Given a test key is already present in the shared run-scoped quarantine memo, when that test fails again at the regression gate, then it is relabeled `flaky-test` without a new probe invocation.
Given at least one test is quarantined during deferred regression, when `runDeferredRegression` returns, then the result includes the quarantine report with quarantined keys and reasons.

routing.reasoning: Although it changes an important flow, the work stays inside the existing deferred-regression module and DI seam, with behavior covered by current unit tests.

analysis:
Feature scope is an enhancement to the existing verification and rectification pipeline, not a greenfield subsystem. The main impact areas are the verification barrel and executor, test-runner parsing/detection types, smart-runner mapping helpers, story-orchestrator rectification, deferred regression, and config merge/schema paths. `TestFailure` already carries the identity the spec needs: `file`, `testName`, `error`, and `stackTrace` in [src/test-runners/types.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/test-runners/types.ts):9, and the parser can emit `file: "unknown"`, which makes some failures inherently unprobeable by design in `src/test-runners/parser.ts:136`, `src/test-runners/parser.ts:199`, and `src/test-runners/parser.ts:428`.

Framework detection already exists and matches the feature design. `Framework` is an open union of `"bun" | "jest" | "vitest" | "pytest" | "go" | "unknown"` and `detectFramework(output)` is the SSOT in [src/test-runners/detector.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/test-runners/detector.ts):13 and [src/test-runners/detector.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/test-runners/detector.ts):77. The probe should reuse that rather than infer frameworks from configured commands, because regression/full-suite failures already flow through raw output.

The execution seam for isolated probe subprocesses is already available. `executeWithTimeout(command, timeoutSeconds, env?, options)` shells through `_executorDeps.spawn`, supports `cwd`, `shell`, `gracePeriodMs`, and `drainTimeoutMs`, and returns environmental timeout results with `success: false` and `countsTowardEscalation: false` in [src/verification/executor.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/verification/executor.ts):12 and [src/verification/executor.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/verification/executor.ts):66. That seam makes `flake-probe.ts` straightforward to unit test without new infrastructure.

Verification exports need extension. The barrel currently only exports `types`, `executor`, `runners`, and `rectification` in [src/verification/index.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/verification/index.ts):8, so both `runFlakeProbe` and `triageFlakyFindings` require new barrel entries to satisfy the spec’s importability ACs.

Finding conversion already emits stable test-failure findings and leaves room for a new `flaky-test` category. `testFailureToFinding()` maps runner failures to `source: "test-runner"`, `severity: "error"`, `category: "failed-test"`, and `rule: failure.testName` in [src/findings/adapters/test-failure.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/findings/adapters/test-failure.ts):4. `Finding.category` is explicitly free-form, not a closed enum, in [src/findings/types.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/findings/types.ts):69 and [src/findings/types.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/findings/types.ts):101, so relabeling to `flaky-test` is backward-compatible at the type level. The implementer should keep downstream branching on `category`, not `meta`, because `meta` is forensic data only per the spec.

The baseline pre-existing-test check should reuse the existing ADR-009 helpers, not inline filename heuristics. `resolveTestFilePatterns(config, workdir, packageDir)` already centralizes test classification and package-relative monorepo handling in [src/test-runners/resolver.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/test-runners/resolver.ts):121, and `mapSourceToTests()` / `importGrepFallback()` already provide source-to-test mapping in [src/verification/smart-runner.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/verification/smart-runner.ts):136 and [src/verification/smart-runner.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/verification/smart-runner.ts):210. Existing unit coverage for those helpers is already extensive in `test/unit/verification/smart-runner-discovery.test.ts:15`, `test/unit/verification/smart-runner-packageprefix.test.ts:25`, and `test/unit/test-runners/resolver.test.ts:44`, so the new triage layer should compose them rather than fork their logic.

Config work is additive but not limited to schema defaults. `ExecutionConfigSchema` currently defines `rectification`, `regressionGate`, `smartTestRunner`, and other execution settings in [src/config/schemas-execution.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/config/schemas-execution.ts):100. `testPatternConfigSelector` already selects `execution`, `project`, and `quality` in [src/config/selectors.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/config/selectors.ts):80, so triage can probably consume the existing slice. The main compatibility risk is package-level merge behavior: `mergePackageConfig()` deep-merges `execution.worktreeDependencies`, `execution.smartTestRunner`, and `execution.regressionGate`, but would currently overwrite a new `execution.flakeDetection` subtree unless `src/config/merge.ts` is updated alongside the schema; see [src/config/merge.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/config/merge.ts):71.

Story-orchestrator integration points are concrete and already structured around findings. `gatherRectificationFindings()` collects findings from validation phases unless `shouldSkipPhaseForRectification()` suppresses the full-suite gate because the verifier already passed in [src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts):16 and [src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts):27. `runRectification()` seeds the fix cycle from `gatherRectificationFindings()` or overrides in [src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts):70. The safest insertion point is after full-suite-gate findings are extracted but before those findings seed the fix cycle.

The phase-eval logic is a second required modification point. `gateFailureKeys()` currently includes every `test-runner` finding as `${file}::${rule}` without category filtering in [src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts):106. `gateRegressedAfterRectification()` treats empty-key or `::` keyless failures as regressions in [src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts):142, so excluding `flaky-test` must be done without weakening keyless execution-failure handling. Existing unit coverage for these helpers lives in [test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator-carveout-staleness.test.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator-carveout-staleness.test.ts):71.

Deferred regression is the highest-risk integration because it currently parses failures, extracts failing test files, attributes them to stories, emits regression events, and dispatches rectification based on all parsed failures. `buildRegressionFindings()` maps parsed failures directly to `failed-test` findings in [src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts):41, `_regressionDeps` is the existing DI seam in [src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts):60, and `runDeferredRegression()` extracts `testFilesInFailures` and attributes every failing test file before fix-cycle dispatch in [src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts):321 and [src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.ts):353. Triage must run before story attribution or affected-story emission; otherwise quarantined flakes still trigger blame and fix cycles.

Current test coverage is a strong base for extension. Regression behavior is already heavily unit-tested in [test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.test.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-regression.test.ts):13 and attribution-specific behavior in `test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-regression-attribution.test.ts:13`. Test-failure finding conversion is covered in [test/unit/findings/adapters/test-failure.test.ts](/Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax/test/unit/findings/adapters/test-failure.test.ts):5. Smart-runner and resolver helpers already have focused suites, so the new feature should add `flake-probe` and `flake-triage` unit suites plus targeted extensions to existing orchestrator/regression suites rather than inventing new integration harnesses.

Backward compatibility and migration are simple: there is no persisted state, no data migration, and the default `execution.flakeDetection.enabled = true` changes runtime behavior only for pre-existing tests that fail and then pass isolated re-runs. `enabled: false` must preserve today’s pipeline behavior exactly. The biggest regression risks are false quarantine from bad baseline detection, double-probing the same test without shared memoization, and accidentally suppressing real gate failures by filtering on `source === test-runner` alone instead of `category === failed-test`. Monorepo compatibility depends on updating deep-merge behavior for the new execution sub-object, even though this repo is currently treated as single-package by the spec.
